query: How is similarity between two embeddings measured?
reference_answer: Similarity is usually measured with cosine similarity, which compares the angle between the two vectors.

query: How does Qdrant organize the vectors it stores?
reference_answer: Qdrant stores vectors in named collections and attaches JSON payloads to every point.

query: What goes wrong when chunks are too large?
reference_answer: The embedding averages too many ideas and retrieval precision drops.
Overlap means consecutive chunks share a band of words, so sentences cut at a boundary stay intact and facts that straddle two chunks are not lost.
Sentence-aware chunking splits on sentence boundaries instead of word counts, keeping every chunk grammatically complete.

query: Which metrics are used to evaluate retrieval quality?
reference_answer: Retrieval quality is evaluated with recall at k and mean reciprocal rank against a golden set of questions.

query: How does rate limiting work at the API gateway?
reference_answer: Rate limiting uses a sliding window per API key and rejects requests once the window budget is exhausted.

query: When is the semantic cache invalidated?
reference_answer: Cached entries expire after a time-to-live and the whole cache is invalidated whenever a new document is uploaded.

query: How can a single request be traced across all the services?
reference_answer: Every request receives an X-Request-ID header, so one request can be traced across all services in the logs.
